messages.content: Write a short announcement for a new feature in a note-taking app: offline sync. Around 200 words.

Clean through the slopwatch gate. 201 words:

## Offline sync

Offline sync is live on desktop, iOS, and Android as of today.

Until now, notes you wrote without a connection stayed on the device that made them. Open the app on your laptop after a flight and yesterday's scribbles were still on your phone. Edit the same note in two places and you got a second copy with "conflict" in the title.

That changes with this release. Every edit made offline is written to a local log and replayed against the server when you reconnect. Edits to different parts of a note merge on their own. When two people genuinely change the same paragraph, we keep both versions and show them side by side so you pick, rather than guessing for you and burying the loser in a duplicate file.

The sync queue survives a force-quit and a reboot. There is nothing to turn on and no separate offline mode to remember to enter, though you can watch the queue drain from the status dot in the sidebar if you want to.

Notebooks over 2 GB sync their most recent 90 days first, then backfill. We are working on making that window configurable.

Bug reports go to support@example.com.

Two placeholders to swap: the 2 GB / 90 day backfill numbers and the support address. The conflict-handling paragraph assumes you keep both versions rather than last-write-wins; if your implementation does the latter, that sentence needs rewriting.
Add a paragraph about what happens when two devices edit the same note offline.

Clean through the gate. Add this after the paragraph on conflict handling ("...burying the loser in a duplicate file."):

Two devices, one note, both offline. Whichever one reconnects first replays its log and lands its edits. The second device replays on top of that. If the two sets of edits touch different paragraphs, you end up with both. If they touch the same lines, you get the side-by-side picker on whichever device you open next, and your choice syncs back out to the other one. A device that stays offline for a month is fine. Its queue replays in order when it comes back, and the picker waits for you then instead of the note being settled in its absence.

This brings the piece to about 300 words, so if 200 was a hard ceiling, the paragraph about the 2 GB / 90 day backfill is the one I would cut for it.

Two things it assumes: that replay is ordered per device and that a long-idle queue never expires server-side. If old queued edits are dropped after some window, the last two sentences are wrong and should say what the window is instead.
The feature is now called "local-first sync". Update the text.

I changed the heading and the opening line only. The word "offline" still appears four times in the body, but as a description of the state a device is in, not as the feature's name — "notes you wrote without a connection", "every edit made offline", "no separate offline mode". Those read correctly under the new name. If the rename is meant to push "offline" out of the vocabulary entirely, say so and I will rework those sentences too; that is a heavier edit than a find-and-replace, since "local-first mode" is not a thing a user enters.

The two placeholders still stand: the 2 GB / 90 day numbers and the support address.
